On the second point (qualify the no-retry guidance): keeping it. The 413s this handles are a request over a hard size or per-request token limit (Groq: `Limit 8000, Requested 10974`; Anthropic: body over its byte limit). Those fail the same way every time the same request is sent, which is why it is "Client retry: No" alongside the 400 rows. A temporary 413 from an OpenAI-compatible backend is hypothetical, and a transient refusal belongs on 429, which already keeps `Retry-After`. The wording in the routing table now says "sending it again unchanged does not help", which is the claim we can stand behind.

Not changing this here. The completion routes have never applied `hide_alias_target` to a relayed provider message: the 400, 404 and 429 relays in `classify_provider_error` reach the caller unchanged there too, and only the pass-through routes (`_passthrough.py`) rewrite the target.
